samples.summary: Design doc's stated invariant ("there is no second way to write a page setup") is now false, and the doc was not updated
samples.evidence: docs-pagination.md:346-351 states that a page-setup write "is not a thin pass-through to the store" because it also needs `docStore.snapshot()`, `doc.refresh()`, layout invalidation and a repaint, and that ruler + `EditorAPI.setPageSetup` "both now share the single `writePageSetup` path inside `initialize()` — there is no second way to write a page setup." This delta adds a second, blessed write path: `guardedSetPageSetup` in packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2884-2896 calls `docStore.setPageSetup(resolvePageSetup(setup))` directly and deliberately skips snapshot/refresh/invalidate/render ("it deliberately does not snapshot or repaint"). The canonical pagination design doc is not touched by the PR, so the documented architecture and the code now disagree about how many page-setup write paths exist.

samples.summary: The guarded store write validates but produces editor state the rest of the page-setup pipeline assumes cannot happen (store written, view/undo not updated)
samples.evidence: `guardedSetPageSetup` performs the same validation and `resolvePageSetup` copy as `writePageSetup` (editor.ts:2078-2090) but omits `docStore.snapshot()`, `doc.refresh()`, `invalidateLayout()` and `render()`. The result is a supported, validated API (`editor.getStore().setPageSetup(...)`, now covered by a passing test at packages/docs/test/view/editor-page-setup.test.ts:344) that persists new geometry into the CRDT while the local editor keeps rendering the old paper size and the change is not a single undo step. Two half-duplicated write paths with different post-conditions is exactly what the pagination design doc argued against; if the intent is only to *guard* the escape hatch, delegating to `writePageSetup` (or refusing the write outright) would give one answer instead of two.

samples.summary: The guarded store enforces read-only for exactly one of ~40 DocStore mutators, so the read-only invariant the new test claims to close is still bypassable through the same object
samples.evidence: The new read-only test (packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts:325-338) asserts that `editor.getStore().setPageSetup()` is neutered in read-only, on the stated rationale that "`getStore()` is public too" and a viewer could otherwise write the document through it. But the proxy (editor.ts:2899-2915) special-cases only `setPageSetup`; every other member is bound and passed straight through. `DocStore` (packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:11-146) exposes `setDocument`, `replaceDocument`, `insertBlock`, `deleteBlock`, `insertText`, `deleteText`, `applyStyle`, `applyBlockStyle`, `setHeader/setFooter`, `setDocStyles`, `undo`/`redo`, table mutators, etc. — all reachable unguarded from a read-only editor via `getStore()`. If the read-only guarantee is an editor invariant rather than a per-method one (the argument the diff's own comments make), the fix leaves the door open for every write except the one with a test, and the new test advertises a guarantee the object does not provide.

samples.summary: Proxy + memoized bind cache is heavy machinery for a one-method guard; a narrowed read-facing return type would fit the actual consumers
samples.evidence: All in-repo consumers of `getStore()` use read-only members: `getDocument()` (docs-export-button.tsx:53), `snapshot()` (docs-find-bar.tsx:56), `canUndo()` (harness/hunt/bridge.ts:386) and an optional `fonts` registry (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:470). Narrowing `EditorAPI.getStore()`'s declared return type to those readers would remove the bypass by construction at the API boundary, instead of adding a ~60-line proxy with a per-function bind cache inside an already very large view file. This is an approach/taste point, not a behavioral defect.

verdict.reason: The proxy really does guard only `setPageSetup` (editor.ts:2899-2915), so the reviewer's mechanical reading is correct — but the defect it infers is not blocking under the design-fit rubric. (a) The repo never asserts a store-level read-only invariant: editor.ts:3955-3958 states read-only is "a client-side convenience — the store/server remains the authoritative write boundary for viewer share tokens", and the very test file cited says the same at lines 286-289. `getDoc()` (editor.ts:2919) hands out the raw mutable `Doc` whose own mutators (model/document.ts:260,277,407,599) are unguarded by design, so completing the store proxy would not close the described door at all. (b) The authoritative guard exists server-side: yorkie-auth.controller.ts:164-204 denies `rw` verbs to non-editor share links (line 200), so a viewer writing through `getStore()` cannot persist to collaborators. (c) No acceptance criterion is touched: the issue's criteria (todo md:47-58) are the Page Setup dialog, MD/TXT export, and the format-painter toggle; the same doc records completeness of the read-only allowlist as a deliberately deferred known limitation (line 114). No duplicated logic, no Non-Goal breached, no user-visible loss of the stated outcome — cost stays inside the codebase's own tidiness, i.e. minor, which does not block.
